mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, thereby driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward 20-day returns do not exceed an 8% annualized return during periods when UNRATE is below 5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 5.5% may signal monetary tightening, leading to decreased liquidity and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the cases when FEDFUNDS > 5.5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2 percentage points in the past month signals strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward 60-day returns do not exceed the historical mean during periods when INDPRO increases by more than 2 percentage points, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% in the past quarter signals economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the cases when GDPC1 contracts by more than 0.5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points in the past month, coupled with a decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 10,000, signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the cases when UNRATE rises by more than 0.2pp and PAYEMS declines by more than 10k, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 320, coupled with an increase in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5%, signals tightening monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive when CPIAUCSL > 320 and FEDFUNDS > 5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 4.5% during a monetary easing cycle signals increased liquidity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward 60-day returns do not exceed the historical mean during periods when FEDFUNDS is below 4.5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in the past month signals strong demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 forward 20-day returns do not exceed an 8% annualized return during periods when HOUST increases by more than 5%, this hypothesis is falsified.
